opener_concept: Token-bag inheritance: each Bb parent passes one of two tokens (B or b) at random; the four equally likely pairs ARE the Punnett square, and 1 of 4 (bb) is the recessive quarter.

board_neutral: No board named; no equation-sheet claims. Punnett-square skill is identical across AQA/Edexcel/OCR. Notation simplified to plain letters where it aids clarity.
tier_ladder: Bronze = read a given cross and count; Silver = derive the cross and scale a fraction to a population; Gold = codominance/incomplete dominance, sex linkage, blood groups, reverse reasoning. Existing bank already matched this ladder; no reordering.
notes: This lesson is Punnett-square probability, not a formula lesson, so the science 'equation/unit-conversion' walk ritual maps to build-grid -> count -> convert-to-percentage-or-population -> check. No equations, units to convert, circuits, or rate charts apply. Completion boundary (phase:substitute) placed after the grid is built and counted; student computes the conversion and the sum-to-four check.
